facts: A signature says who published a package but not what is inside it, so a signed binary can still ship a vulnerable library. [L7]
An attestation is a structured statement such as an SBOM, provenance or scan result, bound to the manifest digest the signature covers. [L9]
ocx package attest publishes attestations through the same keyless pipeline as signing, and sbom reads them back. [L9]

Attach has two shapes, and OCX picks one from what it sees in the environment rather than from a flag. [L15]
attest and push --sbom sign when a signing identity is visible, otherwise they attach the document raw and say so. [L18]
push --sbom attaches the SBOM in the same operation as the push, as sugar for attest --type cyclonedx on that digest. [L23]

sbom resolves one of two modes per invocation, Demand or Permissive, and states which one it used. [L62]
Demand mode lists only documents that passed the full signature pipeline and refuses unsigned attachments outright. [L64]
Permissive mode runs no cryptography, and every document it returns is reported verified false with no signer identity. [L65]
With no flags and no matching policy the read runs in Permissive mode; a matching policy or identity flags selects Demand. [L69]
--verify with no identity source is a usage error, exit 64, rather than a silent fall back to permissive. [L78]
